hints: The graph is acyclic, so process vertices after all their outgoing neighbors.
Store a bitset of reachable vertices for each vertex.
Start with the vertex itself and OR in each outgoing neighbor's bitset.
analogy: Each node collects the destination lists of the nodes it can visit directly.
example: With edges 1->2 and 2->3, reachable counts are 3, 2, 1.
algorithm: Topologically sort the DAG. Process vertices in reverse order, setting their own bit and ORing in the reachability bitset of each outgoing neighbor. Count set bits for each answer.
correctness: Every path from a vertex is either empty or begins with one outgoing edge. Reverse topological order has already computed every neighbor's complete set, so their union plus the vertex is exact.
complexity: For n vertices, m edges and machine word size w, O((n+m)*ceil(n/w)) word operations and O(n*ceil(n/w)) words of space.
